summary: A Cal Fire-design enclosed tower in Humboldt Redwoods State Park, built about 1957-58 on the site of an older one; not operational in 2014, current staffing unconfirmed.

facts.design: Octagonal CalFire-design cab with catwalk on a 29 ft enclosed steel tower
facts.status_note: NHLR lists it as an accessible lookout and Peakbagging.com says it is in good shape. In September 2014 the Mattole Restoration Council reported it not operational; no later staffing report was found.

staffing.status: unconfirmed after 2014; a 2014 repair project aimed at overnight staffing

access.note: NHLR says it is accessible to the public via a trail. These sources do not say whether the cab may be entered or climbed.

visit.trail_note: Hike or bike about 6 to 7 miles. Sources differ: a 7-mile Grasshopper Peak trail (Mattole Restoration Council) versus about 6 miles of good road from the north side (Peakbagging.com).

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire)

Lee Ball assigned to the station, with trailer quarters from June 3; relieved of duties a month early in October
Build year per NHLR, Mattole Restoration Council and Peakbagging.com; the 1957 clipping suggests construction began in 1957
Mattole Restoration Council reported the lookout not operational and began a repair project whose goal was overnight staffing for the 2014 fire season

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, the Mattole Restoration Council and Peakbagging.com all give 1958. A May 1957 clipping describes a new tower being built on the site of an older one declared unsafe, and a 1967 clipping says the lookout was built ten years earlier. Treated as built 1957-58; the story gives both.
NHLR gives 3,379 ft (1,030 m); the Mattole Restoration Council gives 3,381 ft. The story says about 3,380 ft.

notes_for_editor: Build date is contested (1957 clipping vs 1958 in three sources); the story says so. The Living New Deal page (livingnewdeal.org/sites/grasshopper-peak-fire-lookout-humboldt-redwoods-state-park-ca/) returned HTTP 403 and was not used, though a search snippet describes CCC crews building a road and a stone tower on the peak; worth checking if a 1930s build is to be claimed. firelookout.org lists a FFLOS US 1851, CA 46 entry named Grasshopper Mountain with status Gone; not resolved, and the story does not rely on it. An FFLA Facebook snippet mentions new cameras on Grasshopper Peak 1 and 2 (not opened). Current staffing and whether the cab is open to visitors are unknown.
